To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ParaDiS networks allow to run neural networks on various configurations of devices without any need for retraining.

ParaDiS networks are: (i) distributable among various device configurations, (ii) not retrained, (iii) not losing accuracy as compared to individually trained models and (iv) achieving similar or even better accuracy than the individually trained models.
ParaDiS networks allow instant adaptation to any device configuration and achieve the same accuracy as the individual models.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new neural network architecture, ParaDiS, which is able to adapt its structure and weights to the available resources, without retraining, and to achieve similar or better accuracy compared to individual models.
a novel approach to parallel processing in edge devices that allows to achieve better performance and accuracy, while reducing the communication load.
a novel framework for training neural networks for multiple device configurations, which is able to achieve high accuracy and low latency in a variety of deployment scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ParaDiS networks are a very good trade-off between accuracy and efficiency in the context of parallelly distributable neural networks.
ParaDiS networks achieve the best trade-off between accuracy and efficiency among the state of the art methods.
ParaDiS networks are more accurate and more efficient than both individually trained distributed models as well as universally slimmable ones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ParaDiS networks are the best of both worlds, i.e., they are both distributable and slimmable.
ParaDiS networks are able to provide a better tradeoff between accuracy and latency than other existing methods for parallelly distributable neural networks.
ParaDiS neural networks allow to achieve similar or better accuracy with less latency, less communication load and less memory consumption as compared to the individual models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the common belief, distributable neural networks are possible, and they can achieve similar accuracy to the non-distributable ones.
ParaDiS networks can be trained once and used to run in parallel on various devices without retraining, thus reducing significantly the training cost.
ParaDiS networks are a good trade-off between the flexibility and the accuracy of distributed and slimmable networks, respectively.
